issue.title: edit: writing a key under a JSON array turns the array into an object and drops its entries
issue.body:
`setJSONBytes` (internal/edit/json.go:123) treats an array met on the key path as a plain value and replaces it with an object.

Reproduced on main: setting `customModels.1` on

```json
{"customModels":[{"model":"mine"}]}
```

gives `{"customModels":{"1":{…}}}`. The user's own entry is lost and the app can no longer read the field. A missing or empty array (`[]`) turns into `{"0":{…}}` the same way.

Found while reviewing magpie-community/plugins#239 (Tuanjie Cowork stores its models in `settings.json` `customModels[]`). Any agent descriptor that writes a numeric key under an array is affected.

Expected: a numeric key under an array indexes it: replacing at an index that exists, appending at `len`, refusing past it. Never turn the array into an object, and never drop an element the user wrote.

comments.body:
Verified the maintainer's repro on upstream `e4ac5e87` before touching anything: `SetJSON` with `customModels.1` on `{"customModels":[{"model":"mine"}]}` produces `{"customModels":{"1":{…}}}` — the array is replaced and the user's entry is gone. The spec implemented here is the maintainer's, exactly: a numeric key under an array replaces at an index that exists, appends at `len`, refuses past it; the array never becomes an object and no element is dropped.

Branch: [`hunt48-a-edit-array`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt48-a-edit-array), one commit on top of upstream `e4ac5e87`; the patch below applies with `git am`.

## What changed

All in `internal/edit/json.go`:

- `setJSONBytes` (json.go:124): when the deepest existing prefix on the key path is an array and the next key is numeric, the write goes to `setArrayElem` instead of falling into the scalar branch that replaced the array. An exact path that *names* the array still replaces it wholesale, as before.
- `setArrayElem` (json.go:154): the index semantics. `idx < len` reaching this function is refused (an existing element is normally resolved earlier in the walk — only a key gjson can't read as an index, like a leading zero, lands here), `idx == len` appends via `insertElem`, `idx > len` returns an error and the file is left untouched. A non-numeric key under an array is refused the same way — today's code silently turns the array into an object for that case too.
- `insertElem` (json.go:274): appends one element before the closing `]`, matching the file's indentation (and its compact style when there is none), reusing the machinery `insertKey` uses for objects.
- `nest` (json.go:192): keys created from scratch now build an array for a numeric part instead of `{"0":…}` — index `0` only, since the array starts empty; anything else is refused as past its end. A numeric key under an object stays an object key.
- `matchBrace` was parameterized into `matchPair` so the `]` of an array can be matched too; `matchBracket` (json.go:350) is the array form. Behavior for existing callers is unchanged.

## Red before the fix

New table test `TestJSONSetArrayIndex` (`internal/edit/json_array_set_test.go`) on the base commit: 8 of 12 rows fail — all three append rows (including into `[]` and a compact file), the missing-key row (produces `{"customModels":{"0":{…}}}`), and all three refusal rows (no error, plus the corruption). The 4 green rows lock in what already worked: replacing an element at its index, writing deeper into one, and a numeric key under an object staying a key.

## Verification

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package | `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./internal/edit/` | ok |
| Callers of edit | `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./internal/settings/ ./internal/provider/` | ok, ok |
| Format | `gofmt -l internal/edit/` | empty |
| Vet | `GOOS=darwin/linux/windows go vet -tags nogui ./internal/edit/` | clean ×3 |
| Build | `GOOS=darwin/linux/windows go build -tags nogui -o /dev/null .` | ok ×3 (darwin prints a pre-existing cgo `-Wenum-conversion` warning from `internal/gui/trayimage_darwin.go`) |

Ablation: with the test kept and only `internal/edit/json.go` restored from upstream, the same 8 rows fail again with the array→object corruption; restore the fix and the package is green. Mutations: dropping the past-len check (growing the array with zero values instead) turns `refuse past the length` red; widening the new array branch to objects turns `a numeric key under an object stays a key` red. Both reverted.

## Siblings

I looked for existing callers that write numeric keys; none do, so no in-repo behavior changes:

- `internal/agent/droid.go:181` writes the whole `customModels` array under its exact path — that stays a wholesale replace, untouched by the new branch.
- `internal/agent/agy.go` (`customModelsConfig.customModels`) and `internal/library/pimcp.go` (`mcpServers.<name>`), `internal/library/mcp_tools_off.go` (`tools.<k>`), `internal/library/hooks.go` (`hooks.<event>`), `internal/provider/claude_proxy_env.go` (`env.<KEY>`), `internal/agent/claude.go` (`env.<NAME>`) — all string keys under objects; unchanged.
- The reader side already handles arrays: `internal/sessions/droid.go:301` walks `customModels` with `gjson.ForEach` — which is exactly what breaks today once a write has mangled the array into an object.

## Not verified

- No real Tuanjie Cowork plugin was run; the `settings.json` `customModels[]` shape comes from the linked plugin issue (magpie-community/plugins#239).
- `SetJSONItem` (top-level array files like VS Code's chatLanguageModels.json) is a separate where-matched mechanism and is not exercised by this change beyond the package's existing tests.

**AI**: written with an AI coding agent; I've read the whole diff and can answer questions on it myself. The model name is in the commit's trailer.

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/1805ff94340887ce329ca5ec2d198c3e80e50671

`edit.SetJSON` and its preview (`PatchJSON`) now index arrays instead of replacing them with objects. An existing element is replaced at its index; the index at the array length appends; past-end and nonnumeric array paths return an error without writing the file. Missing numeric parents start at index zero, while numeric keys under an existing object stay object keys. The existing exact-path whole-array replacement still works. The shared config-editing contract is documented in agent-wiring.

Adapted from ggbdpq's 2dc57469a7ac0fe74927d1031b164f7dcf823e8d, with co-author credit. I also exercised JSONC appends: the community implementation failed for an empty array containing a comment, a trailing comma, and a line comment after the last element. This version inserts using the parsed last element's offset and the existing `nextToken` helper, preserving existing elements/comments and supporting trailing commas and CRLF without adding a bracket parser or dependency.

Regression evidence: restoring the old runtime source with the new tests reproduces the array-to-object corruption and silently accepted out-of-bounds writes. Fixed JSON/SetJSON/PatchJSON test families pass with `-race -count=5`. Tests cover replacement, deep writes, append, empty/missing arrays, rejected paths, existing object numeric keys, compact files, JSONC comments/trailing commas/CRLF, nested arrays, equal preview/saved bytes, and unchanged files when a later key in a multi-key edit is refused.

At this exact committed head all seven acceptance checks passed with Go 1.26.8 and an isolated HOME: native/Linux/Windows vet and builds, plus `go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m` (69 packages passed). Combined branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-q

No real Tuanjie Cowork plugin or installed agent config was used; this verifies the reported public edit API on temporary files. Cross-OS vet/builds are not native Windows/macOS runtime checks. No GUI assets changed and no upstream PR opened.

Verified https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/1805ff94340887ce329ca5ec2d198c3e80e50671 by cherry-picking it onto upstream/main `63be4771` and ablating the product change on Windows (Go with pinned GOPATH/GOMODCACHE/GOCACHE).

The commit adapts the proposed fix faithfully and extends it where the proposal was weak. `setArrayElem`, `arrayIndex` and the `nest` rework are carried over as-is (same spec: replace at an existing index, append at the length, refuse past-end and non-numeric array paths without writing, missing numeric parents start at index 0, numeric keys under an existing object stay keys, exact-path whole-array replacement untouched). The one rewritten piece is `insertElem`: the proposal located the closing bracket itself, which corrupts appends into JSONC arrays (a comment inside an empty array, a trailing comma, a line comment after the last element — all five of those rows fail against the proposal's code); this version appends at the parsed last element's offset and reuses `nextToken`, keeping comments, trailing commas and CRLF, with no second indexer. Preview consistency holds structurally: `SetJSON` and `PatchJSON` both funnel into the one `setJSONBytes`, and the new `TestJSONSetArrayComments` asserts `bytes.Equal(preview, saved)` per case.

Ablation, `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run TestJSONSetArray ./internal/edit`, with `internal/edit/json.go` reverted to `63be4771` and the tests kept — the maintainer's repro is the `append_at_the_length` row (`customModels.1` on a one-element array):

```
--- FAIL: TestJSONSetArrayIndex/append_at_the_length (0.01s)
    json_array_set_test.go:127: got:
        {
          "customModels": {
            "1": {
              "model": "other"
            }
          }
        }
```

13 failures: the same 8 of 12 `TestJSONSetArrayIndex` rows the proposal's ablation had (3 append, missing-key, 3 refusals, compact), all 5 `TestJSONSetArrayComments` rows (JSONC), and `TestJSONSetArrayRefusalKeepsAllKeys`. With the fix restored: `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/edit 5.834s` (whole package, `-count=1`).

Attribution, checked in the commit itself: Author `vincent <webmaster@palmit.com.au>`, and the message carries exactly `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

Drift and landing: the commit's parent (`b7726551`, the #3020 commit of the same branch) is 486 commits ahead of `63be4771`, but none of them touch `internal/edit/json.go` — its base blob equals the tip's, and the cherry-pick applied cleanly in all three files (docs line auto-merged). Verified the maintainer's repro on upstream `e4ac5e87` before touching anything: `SetJSON` with `customModels.1` on `{"customModels":[{"model":"mine"}]}` produces `{"customModels":{"1":{…}}}` — the array is replaced and the user's entry is gone. The spec implemented here is the maintainer's, exactly: a numeric key under an array replaces at an index that exists, appends at `len`, refuses past it; the array never becomes an object and no element is dropped.

Branch: [`hunt48-a-edit-array`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt48-a-edit-array), one commit on top of upstream `e4ac5e87`; the patch below applies with `git am`.

## What changed

All in `internal/edit/json.go`:

- `setJSONBytes` (json.go:124): when the deepest existing prefix on the key path is an array and the next key is numeric, the write goes to `setArrayElem` instead of falling into the scalar branch that replaced the array. An exact path that *names* the array still replaces it wholesale, as before.
- `setArrayElem` (json.go:154): the index semantics. `idx < len` reaching this function is refused (an existing element is normally resolved earlier in the walk — only a key gjson can't read as an index, like a leading zero, lands here), `idx == len` appends via `insertElem`, `idx > len` returns an error and the file is left untouched. A non-numeric key under an array is refused the same way — today's code silently turns the array into an object for that case too.
- `insertElem` (json.go:274): appends one element before the closing `]`, matching the file's indentation (and its compact style when there is none), reusing the machinery `insertKey` uses for objects.
- `nest` (json.go:192): keys created from scratch now build an array for a numeric part instead of `{"0":…}` — index `0` only, since the array starts empty; anything else is refused as past its end. A numeric key under an object stays an object key.
- `matchBrace` was parameterized into `matchPair` so the `]` of an array can be matched too; `matchBracket` (json.go:350) is the array form. Behavior for existing callers is unchanged.

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/1805ff94340887ce329ca5ec2d198c3e80e50671

`edit.SetJSON` and its preview (`PatchJSON`) now index arrays instead of replacing them with objects. An existing element is replaced at its index; the index at the array length appends; past-end and nonnumeric array paths return an error without writing the file. Missing numeric parents start at index zero, while numeric keys under an existing object stay object keys. The existing exact-path whole-array replacement still works. The shared config-editing contract is documented in agent-wiring.

Adapted from ggbdpq's 2dc57469a7ac0fe74927d1031b164f7dcf823e8d, with co-author credit. I also exercised JSONC appends: the community implementation failed for an empty array containing a comment, a trailing comma, and a line comment after the last element. This version inserts using the parsed last element's offset and the existing `nextToken` helper, preserving existing elements/comments and supporting trailing commas and CRLF without adding a bracket parser or dependency.

Regression evidence: restoring the old runtime source with the new tests reproduces the array-to-object corruption and silently accepted out-of-bounds writes. The commit adapts the proposed fix faithfully and extends it where the proposal was weak. `setArrayElem`, `arrayIndex` and the `nest` rework are carried over as-is (same spec: replace at an existing index, append at the length, refuse past-end and non-numeric array paths without writing, missing numeric parents start at index 0, numeric keys under an existing object stay keys, exact-path whole-array replacement untouched). The one rewritten piece is `insertElem`: the proposal located the closing bracket itself, which corrupts appends into JSONC arrays (a comment inside an empty array, a trailing comma, a line comment after the last element — all five of those rows fail against the proposal's code); this version appends at the parsed last element's offset and reuses `nextToken`, keeping comments, trailing commas and CRLF, with no second indexer. Preview consistency holds structurally: `SetJSON` and `PatchJSON` both funnel into the one `setJSONBytes`, and the new `TestJSONSetArrayComments` asserts `bytes.Equal(preview, saved)` per case.

Upstream's JSONC trailing-comma fix (`5160809d2` follow-up, the `members` check on `insertKey`) exposed the same defect in this patch's `insertElem`: its emptiness check reads the raw text, so an array holding only comments counted as non-empty and the appended element got a leading comma (`[// note, new]`, invalid once comments are stripped). `insertElem` now reads the stripped text the same way `insertKey` does: a comments-only array takes the element before the comment with no comma; a real member still gets `,` appended after the last one.
